title: Learn-to-learn on Arbitrary Textual Conditioning: A Hypernetwork-Driven Meta-gated LLM
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: A biological modulation mechanism that meta-controls base signaling maps onto a hypernetwork that meta-controls a frozen model's gating.
layout: 2 stacked panels, top biology and bottom model, parallel structure with lightning-bolt links
description: The figure has two stacked rounded panels. Each has a colored label bar at the bottom. The top panel, labeled Neuroscience, shows a stimulus feeding classical neurotransmitters (pink box) that lead to synaptic plasticity. A blue neuromodulator box, driven by emotion and cognition, sends arrows labeled gating, guiding and stabilizing back to the neurotransmitters. It also leads to meta-plasticity, and a bracket lists example modulators such as dopamine. A lightning bolt links it to the phrase environmental self-adaptation. The bottom panel, labeled Language Model, mirrors this layout. A query enters a frozen LLM, shown as a stack of FFN blocks with a snowflake icon, and a response comes out. A fire-marked hypernetwork takes a descriptive prompt (conditions such as task, domain, persona and style) and combines its output with layer index embeddings. The result sends adaptive gating arrows into each FFN. A lightning bolt links it to meta-learning.
caption: Paradigm of MeGan analogous to neuro-system. Nueromodulator meta-controls classical neurotransmitters, shaping the synaptic plasticity to meta-plasticity. Similarly, we implement a hypernetwork that converts textual condition inputs into meta signals. These signals are combined with layer index embedding, then meta-control the gating of LLM FFNs.
abstract: Conventional LLMs may suffer from corpus heterogeneity and subtle condition changes. While finetuning can create the catastrophe forgetting issue, application of meta-learning on LLMs is also limited due to its complexity and scalability. In this paper, we activate the meta-signal of $Î²$ within the SwiGLU blocks, resulting in a meta-gating mechanism that adaptively adjusts the nonlinearity of FFN. A hypernetwork is employed which dynamically produces $Î²$ on textual conditions, providing meta-controllability on LLMs. By testing on different condition types such as task, domain, persona, and style, our method outperforms finetuning and meta-learning baselines, and can generalize reasonably on unseen tasks, condition types, or instructions. Our code can be found in https://github.com/AaronJi/MeGan.
